morningLede: The national tape is flat (months-stock 13.4 vs 13.7 a month ago, median asking unchanged at $430k) but underneath it the market has split in two: Sydney's growth basins are carrying 29–34 months of stock with a 39% ask-to-sold gap in Sydney Southwest, while SA and WA sit under 8 months with Adelaide North clearing at essentially the asking rate ($914 ask vs $910 sold $/m²). With the negative-gearing rotation toward new builds due to pull investor demand into land from late 2026, the question is no longer whether the east-coast overhang clears, but who is priced to catch that bid.
note: House views written each morning by the desk analyst from last night's run. Income and build-cost figures are APPROXIMATE external benchmarks (label them as such, or verify current figures with web search). Land figures are from the certified RLP dataset.

houseViews.view: Price discovery is functionally broken in Sydney's land corridors. The three big basins sit at 28.9–33.7 months of stock; Sydney Southwest is asking $2,105/m² against $1,511/m² certified sold (+39%), and Sydney Northwest has only 191 of 570 listings priced (34%) — vendors withholding price rather than cutting it. The NSW headline improvement (months-stock 16.5→15.3, asking $/m² 1,532→1,474) is mix, not clearance: 264 annual sales against 742 active in Sydney South West is a market on strike. Vendors will capitulate through lot-size compression and incentives before printed asking rates fall.
houseViews.falsifier: Sydney basin priced-share rising above 60% alongside sold $/m² holding within 10% of asking, or corridor months-stock falling below 20 on rising sold counts.

houseViews.view: VIC is 53% of national active listings (6,573 of 12,340) at 17.1 months and still building (16.9 a month ago), with Melbourne Peri-Urban at an extreme 38.5 months. But VIC is also the only deep market that is honestly priced: 95% of listings carry a price (6,275/6,573) and the ask-to-sold gap is a workable 13% ($841 vs $741/m²) versus Sydney's 39%. That makes VIC the mechanical beneficiary of the late-2026 investor rotation into new builds — cheap ($394k median), abundant, and screenable. Position: the overhang caps price growth through mid-2026, but this is inventory digestion, not a NSW-style freeze.
houseViews.falsifier: VIC months-stock pushing past 20 with sold 12m rolling below ~4,000, or the investor rotation failing to lift new-listing absorption by Q1 2027.

houseViews.view: From 1 Jul 2027 negative gearing narrows to new builds and the CGT discount becomes indexation — investors who want the grandfathered/new-build treatment rationally move into land from late 2026. The bid lands where product is titled, priced and cheap: VIC and outer QLD/SA corridors, not Sydney's POA-heavy basins where an investor cannot even screen 66% of Northwest stock. Expect the rotation to compress VIC months-stock before it moves Sydney prices; tight markets (SA 6.2 months, WA 7.9) get the inflation, loose priced markets get the volume.
houseViews.falsifier: No pickup in investor-share of land sales or new-listing absorption in VIC/QLD by Q1 2027, or the policy being amended before commencement.

houseViews.view: Maintained: strong but composition-inflated — the ~28% headline sold-$/m² growth still carries one estate at roughly a third of 2026 sales; like-for-like is ~9.5%. The tightness is real and got marginally tighter: 6.2 months of stock, and Adelaide North is now clearing at the asking rate ($914 ask vs $910 sold $/m², 5.4 months) — a zero-negotiation market, versus a 39% gap in Sydney Southwest. SA rocketships (Roseworthy, Mount Barker, Virginia, Morphett Vale) dominate the movers table, confirming breadth beneath the composition noise.
houseViews.falsifier: Two consecutive months of rising inflow or incentive share, or like-for-like growth converging to zero.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the affordability ceiling remains the central SA risk — the historically cheap state now asks $420k median with the rocketship list showing price defended via lot compression (Roseworthy -47% lot size over 3yrs, Mount Barker -27%, Morphett Vale -33%). Compression is the market's confession that the gross-price ceiling is binding. While stock stays near 6 months the mechanism is deceleration to single digits, not correction — and the late-2026 investor rotation adds a demand leg that delays the reckoning.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months, or sold rates softening two runs in a row, or lot compression stalling while sales volumes fall.

houseViews.view: Updated: the late-stage read strengthens — $/m² is now accelerating, not plateauing (+49.7% prior year, +99.6% last 12 months to $1,027/m², nearly 3x the $344 of three years ago) while lots compressed another 38% in a single year. A market doubling its rate while shrinking its product by a third is borrowing from the price ceiling, not raising it. Position unchanged and higher-conviction: sell stage stock into this rate; do not underwrite englobo at $1,027/m² residuals.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m² keeps rising on sustained volume above ~50 sales per window.

houseViews.view: Updated — the fallen-angel gloom was overdone at the corridor level. Bendigo corridor sits at 8.8 months with 304 annual sales and Ballarat at 10.1 months on 458 sales — both tighter than the VIC state average of 17.1 and healthier than any Melbourne fringe corridor. The suburb-level Bendigo print (-37.6% sold $/m²) is on 7 sales with lot size simultaneously down 37% — small-sample mix, not a collapse. Revised position: regional VIC majors are the stabilised, liquid end of Victoria; the genuine distress lives in Melbourne Peri-Urban (38.5 months) and the coastal/lifestyle belt (Torquay -18.6% over 3yrs, Portarlington -27.3%, San Remo -25.9%).
houseViews.falsifier: Bendigo/Ballarat corridor months-stock rising above 14 or sold volumes falling two consecutive runs.

houseViews.view: New: WA is the momentum market but the tell is where the momentum sits. State stock is tight (7.9 months, listings up 607→732 in a month with asking $/m² up 1,000→1,041) and the rocketship list is WA-heavy — Mandurah is accelerating (+24.4% prior year, +98.6% last 12m to $842/m² with lots down 35% over 3yrs), while Hilbert and Australind show decelerating second derivatives (59→27% and 53→43%). The 20% ask-to-sold gap ($1,041 vs $867/m²) says vendors are pricing the next leg, not the last one. Position: still long the tight-supply story, but the easy repricing is done in Perth metro; the marginal dollar is chasing satellites late.
houseViews.falsifier: WA months-stock rising above 10, or two consecutive rocketship windows where lot compression continues but sold $/m² growth drops below 10%.

houseViews.view: New: QLD's apparent 30-day crash — median asking $539k→$478k, asking $/m² $1,029→$710, listings 758→1,056 — is the 7-Jul universe expansion (948→1,022 suburbs) pulling regional QLD (Townsville at $305k/8.8 months, Gympie, Kingaroy) into the sample, not a repricing. Months-stock at 8.9 and genuine SEQ rocketships (South Ripley +82% last 12m to $1,774/m², Bahrs Scrub +53% to $1,319, Greenbank +57% to $1,373) say the underlying market remains firm. Do not trade the state-level QLD series until the new-suburb cohort matures; trade the corridor and suburb series instead.
houseViews.falsifier: Like-for-like (pre-expansion suburb set) QLD asking or sold $/m² actually falling on the next monthly comparison.

houseViews.view: Retired: the suburb dropped out of the movers and corridor tables this run so the 50% ask-over-sold thesis can no longer be tracked at desk cadence; the falsifier was never triggered. The negotiation-window logic transfers to the broader SA tight-supply view — note that Adelaide North's zero gap ($914 vs $910/m²) shows where SA vendor ambition has already been validated, making unpriced or wide-gap SA satellites the residual acquisition targets.
houseViews.falsifier: n/a — retired on data coverage; re-open if Murray Bridge re-enters the tracked set with a sold-vs-asking gap above 25%.
